function: Sensing-aided beam prediction and future beam tracking at a mmWave basestation serving a drone, selecting codebook beams from camera images, GPS, height, and distance (p. 3-4, 7-9).
system: Basestation 16-element ULA with RGB camera, 64-beam codebook (32 used), 60 GHz; drone transmits through a single antenna element, GPS; OFDM; no RIS (p. 5, 12).
method: Supervised classification: 2-layer MLP on GPS, height, distance; fine-tuned ResNet-50 on images; attention-fusion multimodal model; 2-layer GRU with YOLOv3 features for future beams (p. 8-9, 11-12).
data_channel: Measured DeepSense 6G Scenario 23 (Thude Park drone, 60 GHz): images, GPS, 64-beam power; 8,403 training and 3,602 test samples, 70-30% split (p. 12, 15-16, 18).
test_conditions: Same-scenario 70-30% split; also simulated low-light images, 50-step rollouts beyond 8-sample inputs, height and speed subgroups of the test set (p. 15, 20-22, 26-27).
baselines: Non-learned traditional beam training (exhaustive sweep); learned beam-only GRU for tracking; position-only MLP versus vision and multimodal models; no earlier published predictor re-implemented (p. 9, 17, 23, 25).
metrics: Top-1, top-2, top-3, top-5 beam accuracy; R2 of predicted versus optimal received power; beam training overhead reduction; latency and parameters (p. 17-19, 23).
complexity: Parameters and latency: position MLP 0.8254M, 1.58 ms; vision ResNet-50 23.64M, 5.63 ms; multimodal 25.64M, 6.83 ms (Table 4, p. 23).
openness: Scenario 23 added to the public DeepSense 6G dataset [33]; no code link or URL given (p. 3, 13).
q1_support: p. 12: "mandates the construction of a measurement-based real-world dataset" - measured 60 GHz DeepSense 6G Scenario 23 data (p. 12-13), not a simulated model.
q2_support: p. 15: "partitioning the dataset into training and test sets following a 70-30% distribution" - training and test come from the same Scenario 23; the low-light test applies synthetic image degradation (p. 21), like a perturbation sweep, and the 50-step rollout (p. 26) reuses the same models; no other site, scenario, or band is tested.
q3_support: p. 17: "we compare multiple approaches with traditional beam training as the baseline" - non-learned baseline is exhaustive beam training (32 or 64 measurements versus 3, p. 23); the learned baseline is the beam-only GRU (p. 9); no earlier published learned predictor is re-implemented.
q4_support: p. 23: "23.64M parameters, resulting in a latency of 5.63 ms" - Table 4 also gives 0.8254M and 1.58 ms for position and 25.64M and 6.83 ms for multimodal.
q5_support: p. 3: "Development of the drone communication scenario (Scenario 23) in DeepSense 6G [33], a large-scale dataset" - public DeepSense 6G dataset that the paper extends and uses for training and testing; no explicit URL is given.
notes: Area 6 chosen because the learned beam control serves an aerial (drone) link and 6 outranks 3; area 3 if the reviewer treats the ground basestation to drone link as terrestrial beam prediction. Borderline q2, marked 0: the nearest candidates are the simulated low-light test images (p. 21), read as a perturbation sweep, and the 50-step rollout (p. 26), both on the same scenario; the paper does not say whether the vision model was trained on undegraded images, and the reviewer may count them as new conditions. Borderline q3: the learned baseline is the paper's own conventional beam-only GRU; earlier predictors such as [19], [26] are cited but not compared. Section VIII (p. 24) cites DeepSense Scenario 18 for tracking, apparently a typo for Scenario 23 of Section VI. Table 2 lists 12005 samples under Training while p. 18 gives 8403 train and 3602 test.
